about: What the deploy kit needs that no Worker's config can say (deploy/facts.ts reads it, with the six wrangler.jsonc). Everything a config says (each Worker's name, bindings, required secrets, bucket and queues, Durable Object migrations, and the order its bindings set) is read from the config; the shared apps' signing secrets from the file its workers entry names; the doors' public identity from contract/identity.json. Each entry here carries its reason.

namespaces.why: A config names a KV namespace by an id the account gives when it is made (a placeholder as checked in), never by its title: the kit finds each by its title, or makes it, and fills the id in. One title per binding name: every Worker's CONTROL is the one namespace.

workers.why: What the kit gives a Worker that its config cannot say, by its folder. identity: it serves contract/identity.json, so it deploys with the owner issuer and WorkOS's record (its vars OWNER_ISSUER and UPSTREAM), and mode routes hands it identity.json's routes and contract/egress.json's custom domain. shared_apps: its file of the shared apps, whose signing secrets it holds when each is given (no config requires them: without one, that app's door refuses loudly). clock: it runs the platform canary's clock (doors/src/canary-clock.ts), so it holds the clock's dispatch token and the pager's keys when each is given (contract/canary.json), none required: without the token the clock dispatches nothing. Exactly one Worker serves the identity; a Worker not named here takes none of these.

secret_order.why: The order the kit lists and sets the Workers' secrets in, so the plan names them in it. A config says which secrets its Worker needs, not this order. The codemode Worker holds no secret, so it is not here: its existence is read when it deploys.

retired.why: The Workers the platform no longer has: the one way a platform Worker is deleted, so the cutover manifest names its Workers here. Each is deleted by the deploy step after every Worker is deployed, when the account's Workers listing holds it: by then no Worker of this tree binds it, and Cloudflare refuses the delete while any other Worker still references it (the kit never forces it) and deletes the Worker's own Durable Object namespaces with it. tinyassets-hooks is the code mode Worker's name before its rename: its VMs keep no state, so its objects go with it. An entry is deleted once a deploy has run it.

buckets.why: The R2 buckets the kit makes that no Worker binds, by what each holds (the name its reader takes it by, facts.ts --import), each made by dark's storage step when the account's listing lacks it, as the bound ones are. final_backup holds the off-site copy of the import window's final backup (import-window.yml, mode offsite): kept through the 14-day hold, then deleted with the old stack's final backup, on the founder's word (tasks.md section 9).

bucket_locks.why: The R2 buckets whose every object is kept, unchangeable and undeletable, for so many days, by the binding that binds each: a config names a bucket, not a lock on it. OPERATOR_LOG is the operator channel's audit log (doors/src/operator.ts): each message's acceptance record and answer, kept a year (d3 §G). dark's storage step makes each the bucket's one lock rule, over every object, when the bucket holds no rule or another.

keyrings.why: The keyrings the platform seals stored blobs under, each by the operator op that brings one owner's blobs under its active kid (contract/src/operator-message.ts), which mode rotation asks of every owner the directory lists, and whether the off-account copy holds blobs under it (deploy/offsite.ts copies the files bucket: every generation's root carries the data key wrapped under FILES_KEYRING), so mode retire waits out the copy's versions under a retiring kid. sandboxed: the keyrings whose values live as long as the E2B sandboxes that carry them, which no sweep can bring under a new kid: ROUTING_KEYRING seals each sandbox's route into its E2B metadata once, at its create (E2B changes no sandbox's metadata after, and keeps a paused sandbox indefinitely), and that sandbox's lease's egress and sync tokens, which live in it, are minted no earlier; a socket ticket lives 30 s. So mode retire takes its old kids out only once every route E2B holds, running or paused, opens under the stored ring alone (deploy.ts routesHeld). A keyring in neither (OPERATOR_KEYRING, the kit's MAC key) strands nothing when a kid goes.

made.why: The platform-generated secrets by the kind of initial value each needs: token a random URL-safe token, keyring a first keyring in keyring-new's shape (rotated only by adding a key). A config names a secret, not how its value is made; every other secret comes from its vendor or a shared app.
